Welcome Back to All Saints – Autumn Term 2026
Dear Parents and Carers,
A very warm welcome back to All Saints as we begin a new academic year together. We hope that all our families have enjoyed the very hot summer break and are feeling refreshed and ready for another exciting year of learning and growth.
We are delighted to welcome back our well-established families and extend an especially warm welcome to all the children and families who are new to All Saints. We hope that you will quickly feel part of our caring and inclusive school community.
Our Christian value for Autumn Term 1 is Respect. Throughout this half term, we will be helping our children to think about what respect looks like in their relationships, their learning and the way they care for themselves, others and our school community.
We also look forward to continuing our close relationship with All Saints Church throughout the year, strengthening the important links between our school, church, families and wider community.
Staying Connected: Good communication between home and school is very important to us. Each parent and carer will be invited to join our ClassDojo messaging system, helping you to stay connected with your child’s class and receive important information and updates.
Meet the Teacher Meetings: As always, over the next two weeks we will be holding our Meet the Teacher meetings, class by class, from Tuesday to Thursday. These are an opportunity to meet your child’s teacher, hear about the year ahead and find out how we can work together to support your child’s learning.
A Special Year for Year 6: For our Year 6 children and families, this is an especially important and exciting year. Over the coming weeks, families will be embarking on the important task of exploring and choosing secondary schools that are right for their child, ahead of the secondary school application deadline at the end of October. We know this can feel like a big decision, and we will be here to support our Year 6 families through this important stage of their child’s journey.
The staff and I are very happy to be back and are looking forward to everything the new academic year will bring. Thank you, as always, for your continued support and partnership.
We wish all our children and families a happy, successful and enjoyable year ahead.
Our Value is ‘Respect‘
“Do to others as you would have them do to you.”

Tuesday 10th November at 9.30am

Breakfast Club
All Saint’s Breakfast Club:
Breakfast Club is run by the school and costs £3.00 a day. It is open at 7:45am until school starts. This includes a healthy breakfast and supervision and is available to children from All Saint’s from Nursery through to Year 6.
Breakfast Club Includes:
Baked beans or scrambled egg
Water and milk
Free Breakfast provision:
Different from All Saints paid Breakfast Club
The government is planning for all primary schools to offer free breakfast provision from 2027.
From 7th September 2026, our school will be offering a Free Breakfast Provision for pupils in Reception to Year 6. This will replace the current NBCP bagel offer.
The Free Breakfast Provision will run from 8:30am to 9:00am, providing a simple, healthy breakfast such as a toast or cereal and piece of fruit. Water will always be available, and milk may occasionally be offered.
Please note:
This is nota childcare session.
Payment of fees:
Breakfast Club fees are payable weekly in advance via the School Gateway App and bookings are also made on the App. The current cost is £3.00 a day per child. If you require any information please speak to the school office for advice.

Art/DT Overview
Art & Design Technology Overview
At All Saints’, we believe that a high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire and challenge pupils; equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art and design. We have a dedicated art room where children have the opportunity to develop their skills using a range of media and materials. In art, children learn the skills of drawing, painting, printing, collage, textiles and 3D work. Design technology offers the chance to design and build projects using a range of different materials.
Art lessons introduce children to a range of works of art and develop knowledge of the styles and vocabulary used by famous artists. The skills they acquire are applied to their cross-curricular topics, allowing children to use their art skills to explore themes in greater depth and learn about art from a range of different countries and cultures. Children are also given the opportunity to be reflective and evaluate their work, thinking about how they can make changes and develop their mastery of different techniques.
DT lessons provide children with the opportunity to research past and present designs and designers, understanding the impact that different products have had on daily life. When designing, children are encouraged to communicate their ideas through diagrams, mock-ups and prototypes and practice using a range of tools accurately and safely. Children are also encouraged to evaluate and test their ideas and products in relation to the initial design purpose.

Mathematics Overview
Mathematics Overview
At All Saints’, we recognise the varied and diverse applications of mathematics in the real world and strive to support all our children to develop a confident and enthusiastic attitude towards their mathematical learning. Our mathematics curriculum aims to provide all children with a firm foundation for understanding number, reasoning, thinking logically and problem solving. We use the National Curriculum programmes of study as well as mathematics mastery resources to guide our pupils through the crucial stages of mathematical development.
Our approach to teaching encourages a clear focus on mathematical fluency, problem solving, reasoning and the skills of using and applying mathematical understanding. There is a strong emphasis on the development of mental arithmetic skills and providing opportunities for pupils to use and apply mathematics in real life situations. Children are encouraged to talk mathematically and develop their vocabulary through teacher modelling, investigations and talk tasks. Times tables also play an important part in our maths learning, with children developing their fluency and rapid recall of tables up to 12×12 by the end of Year 4.

In Early Years, mathematics is taught through both teacher-led and child-initiated activities. It is consolidated through practical, hands-on experiences, games, group tasks, investigations and a range of real-life contexts which develop both mathematical understanding and problem-solving skills. In Key Stages 1 and 2, children are taught through daily mathematics lessons involving a balanced mix of independent work, paired or group tasks and whole class teaching. As pupils achieve fluency in key skills and mathematical concepts, they move on to applying their understanding through problem solving and reasoning.

PE & Sports Funding
Funding for Primary School PE and Sports
The current Coalition Government has allocated an additional £150 million state funding to all state sector primary teaching establishments for the academic years of 2013 – 2016. The fundamental aim of this grant aid is to further improve the provision and quality of Physical Education (PE) and Sport provided by all primary schools nationally.
The funding is provided jointly by the Departments of Education, Health; Culture Media & Sport and is to be ring fenced thus ensuring that schools spend their grant only upon PE & Sport as well as initiatives that address developing healthy lifestyles in either curricular or extra-curricular settings.
Purpose of funding
It is a mandatory requirement, as authorised by Department of Education (DfE), that all state schools dedicate this funding upon developing their provision of PE and sport, although how they do decide to address this task remains their decision. Science Overview
Our science curriculum
We use Kapow Primary Science from Year 1 to Year 6 as the main resource for teaching the National Curriculum. Teachers adapt its lessons and enquiries to meet the needs of their class and connect learning with our local environment, Forest School, wider curriculum and pupils’ experiences. In Nursery and Reception, science is taught through purposeful play, talk, stories, observation and practical exploration within Understanding the World.
The curriculum builds knowledge in biology, chemistry and physics alongside the skills needed to work scientifically. Important ideas and vocabulary are revisited so pupils can remember more, make connections and explain their thinking with increasing confidence.
What pupils learn to do
observe closely and use equipment safely;
identify, compare, group and classify;
use and understand increasingly precise scientific vocabulary.
Early Years Foundation Stage
In Nursery and Reception, children encounter science mainly through the EYFS area Understanding the World. Experiences are planned across the year and respond to seasonal change, children’s questions and opportunities in the school grounds. Adults model accurate vocabulary and help children observe, compare, predict, test simple ideas and explain what they notice.
My body and senses; familiar materials; autumn and weather; caring for living things.
Animals and their young; ice and melting; light and shadow; changes in the natural world.
Seeds and plant growth; minibeasts and habitats; water and floating; summer observations.
Seasonal change; ourselves and healthy choices; materials and their properties; observing the school environment.
Animals, habitats and life cycles; changing materials; forces through pushes, pulls and movement.
Plants and growth; caring for the environment; shadows and sunlight; simple investigations and recording.
These headings describe the scientific experiences offered through the EYFS curriculum. They are not taught as isolated formal units; learning is woven through provision, stories, outdoor learning and children’s interests.
Science curriculum overview Years 1 to 6
The overview below shows the science content planned for each academic year. The order may be adjusted when this improves links with seasonal opportunities, visits or other curriculum learning, while maintaining full National Curriculum coverage and progression.
Seasonal changes; everyday materials
Sensitive bodies; comparing animals
Introduction to plants; science stories
Habitats and microhabitats
Everyday materials; life cycles and health
Plant growth; plant based materials
Movement and nutrition; forces and magnets
Rocks and soil; light and shadows
Plant reproduction; hand span investigation
Digestion and food; electricity and circuits
States of matter; sound and vibrations
Classification and habitats; liquid flow investigation
Mixtures and separation; properties and changes
Earth and space; life cycles and reproduction
Unbalanced forces; human timeline; asteroid enquiry
Classification; light and reflection
Evolution and inheritance; circuits batteries and switches
Circulation and health; sunglasses investigation
Working scientifically and practical learning
Working scientifically is taught through every science unit rather than as a separate strand. In Years 1 and 2, pupils ask simple questions, observe, classify, test and record. In Years 3 and 4, they select enquiry approaches, make careful measurements, present data and draw conclusions. In Years 5 and 6, they plan enquiries, control variables where appropriate, take increasingly accurate measurements, evaluate evidence and justify conclusions.
Teachers provide regular practical experiences using safe, suitable equipment and the school environment. Pupils also learn that science is carried out by people from many backgrounds and that scientific explanations can change when new evidence becomes available.
Vocabulary reading and communication
Teachers explicitly teach and revisit scientific vocabulary. Pupils use discussion, diagrams, tables, graphs and written explanations to communicate their ideas. Reading supports science through carefully chosen texts and information sources, while practical work gives pupils meaningful contexts in which to use new language.
Inclusion and equality
Science is ambitious and accessible for all pupils, including pupils with SEND, pupils learning English as an additional language and disadvantaged pupils. Teachers maintain the intended scientific learning while adapting explanations, modelling, vocabulary, equipment, recording methods and levels of adult support. Reasonable adjustments and accessible alternatives enable pupils to participate safely in practical work, outdoor learning and visits.
Assessment
Assessment is woven through teaching. Teachers use questioning, discussion, practical work, quizzes and pupils’ recorded outcomes to identify what has been understood and where misconceptions remain. End of unit outcomes, together with ongoing evidence, inform future teaching. Leaders review coverage, progression, pupil work and pupil voice to evaluate the quality and impact of the curriculum.
Finding out more
Parents, carers and members of the public can find out more by contacting the school office and asking to speak with the Science Leader or Headteacher. This overview should be read alongside the whole school Curriculum Policy, Curriculum Map, Accessibility Plan, Equality Policy and Objectives, and SEND Information Report.
Kapow Primary is a commercial teaching resource used by the school. Detailed lesson plans, teaching slides and assessment materials are available to staff through the school subscription and are not reproduced on the public website.

SEND Support
SEND Support
Croydon Drop In Service
This is a well-established, evidence based service delivered in partnership with the school to help support the emotional well-being of the children. It provides 1:1 therapy with a trained counsellor and strives to help build the children’s confidence and resilience. The intervention addresses issues specific to each individual child’s needs. The CDI counsellor and the school SENCo meet on a weekly basis.
Play Therapist
This provides 1:1 support for children using play and arts with an integrative approach. It provides the opportunity to explore emotions/difficulties and challenges in a curious, nurturing and safe place. The therapist also works with parents and school staff offering support. The Therapist and the school SENCo meet on a weekly basis.
Details of the Locality SEND Support way of working
Over the past two years Croydon LA have been introducing a rapid response Locality SEND Support process (LSS) to ensure that SEND support provision in schools for Croydon resident children is robust and consistent. This is being done in order to help local schools be better able to support pupils with SEND and their families. From September 2022 all schools in Croydon who have accepted their invitation to be part of LSS will have the chance to access additional resources to support early intervention. Under LSS, provision for pupils with SEND should therefore improve. LSS will also develop partnerships and networks that support school-led improvement, promote school collaboration and enhance inclusive practice. Existing EHCPs in schools will continue to be honoured and ELPS and Special Schools are outside of this initiative.
